text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 5

The panel's composition tells you almost nothing here. You and the appointee are both women, so an all-female panel gives no basis for a sex-discrimination claim — and raising it would likely read as a weak argument that undermines your credible complaint.

Your real grievance is substantive: on paper you have the stronger academic profile (completed PhD, six papers, four years teaching), and the university has ignored a reasonable request for written reasons for two weeks.

Focus there. Send a firm follow-up citing any statutory or policy right to reasons and appeal deadlines. Ask how "industry experience" was weighted against the advertised criteria. If the criteria were applied inconsistently, that's your case — not the panel's sex.
